healthcareSystem: Public healthcare is available but limited. Hospital Agostinho Neto in Praia is the main facility. Private clinics on Sal and Santiago offer better care for tourists. Smaller islands have only basic health centers.
qualityNotes: Moderate healthcare for a small island nation. Hospitals in Praia and Mindelo handle routine cases. Portuguese is the medical language. Some doctors speak English or French. Serious conditions require evacuation to Lisbon or Dakar.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies open 8am-7pm weekdays, 8am-1pm Saturday. Duty pharmacies (farmácia de serviço) operate after hours on rotation.
pharmacyTips: Pharmacies on Sal, Santiago, and São Vicente are reasonably stocked. Smaller islands have limited options. Portuguese is the primary language. Bring specialty medications from home.
prescriptionRules: Prescriptions required for antibiotics and controlled substances. Portuguese-language prescriptions expected. Many basic medications available OTC.

restrictedMeds.name: Narcotic medications
restrictedMeds.note: Carry a doctor's letter, ideally in Portuguese. Keep in original packaging.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter listing all medications, ideally translated into Portuguese. Keep medications in original packaging. Bring extra supplies for inter-island travel.

travelInsurance.tips: Strongly recommended. Medical evacuation to Lisbon or Dakar may be needed for serious conditions. Ensure coverage includes water sports and hiking activities.

vaccinations.notes: Yellow fever certificate required if arriving from an endemic country. Dengue and Zika have been reported. No malaria risk.

waterNotes: Tap water quality varies by island. Bottled water is recommended, especially on smaller islands. Resorts on Sal and Boa Vista generally provide safe drinking water. Cape Verde is a dry country — water scarcity is common.
foodSafetyTips: Food at restaurants is generally safe. Fresh seafood is a highlight but ensure it is well cooked. Cachupa (national stew) is safe at restaurants. Be cautious with raw shellfish and street food.
medicalTourismNote: Cape Verde is not a medical tourism destination. Patients needing specialist care travel to Lisbon (Portugal) or Dakar (Senegal).
metaDescription: Health guide for Cape Verde (Cabo Verde): emergency numbers, pharmacy tips, restricted medications, vaccinations, water safety tips, and insurance advice.

hospitals.name: Hospital Agostinho Neto
hospitals.notes: Main national hospital. Largest facility in Cape Verde. Portuguese-speaking. Emergency department. Best equipped hospital in the country.

hospitals.name: Hospital Baptista de Sousa
hospitals.notes: Second-largest hospital. Serves São Vicente and surrounding islands. Portuguese-speaking.

hospitals.name: Hospital Regional de Santiago Norte
hospitals.notes: Regional hospital serving northern Santiago. Basic emergency care.

hospitals.name: Delegacia de Saúde de Sal
hospitals.notes: Health center on Sal Island. Basic care for tourists. For serious issues, transfer to Praia or evacuation is needed.

dentalCare.availability: Limited dental care in Praia and Mindelo. Very few options on tourist islands like Sal.
dentalCare.notes: Private dental clinics in Praia offer basic care. Portuguese-speaking. Equipment varies.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: Hospital Agostinho Neto in Praia has dental services. On Sal, ask at the health center for referrals.

mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Very limited. Some Portuguese-speaking counselors in Praia.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are limited. Bring all psychiatric medications from home.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility is limited. Cobblestone streets in historic towns are challenging. Newer resorts on Sal have better accessibility.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Hospital Agostinho Neto has basic wheelchair access. Smaller health centers are less accessible.
accessibilityInfo.transport: No accessible public transport. Taxis available. Inter-island flights are the main transport between islands.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Sal Island resorts have the best accessibility in Cape Verde. Historic towns like Cidade Velha have cobblestone streets. Confirm accessibility with specific hotels before booking.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.testing: Available at hospitals in Praia and Mindelo.
covidStatus.notes: Dengue, sun exposure, and water scarcity are more relevant health concerns for travelers.

insuranceClaimProcess: Hospitals require upfront payment (Cape Verdean Escudo or Euros accepted). Keep all receipts. Documentation may be in Portuguese — request English copies if possible.

commonCosts.note: Estimated typical out-of-pocket costs. Local currency is Cape Verdean Escudo (CVE), pegged to the Euro. Euros widely accepted.

medicalEvacuation.note: Medical evacuation insurance is recommended. Lisbon is the most common evacuation destination due to strong Portuguese ties and direct flights. Las Palmas is closer for emergencies from northern islands.
